scope: Bounded Linux measurement of cosign verification cost with and without a prepared Sigstore trusted root; public keyless-signed image used because private GHCR package reads are only available inside the runner job

subject.reason: public keyless signature from a GitHub Actions workflow, same Sigstore public-good trust path as the private consumer images

observations: Caching the Sigstore TUF material in $HOME does not change verification time: 2.03s cold and 2.03s warm median.
Verifying with a prepared trusted root measured a 1.63s median, a 0.40s reduction against the 2.03s baseline on this host.
Preparing the trusted root costs 1.23s once per job in the unmeasured preparation step and also warms the TUF material used by signing.

steps: Prepare private provenance trust runs cosign initialize, copies the TUF trusted root into RUNNER_TEMP and exports SIGSTORE_TRUSTED_ROOT.
Sign and verify private image provenance passes --trusted-root when SIGSTORE_TRUSTED_ROOT is set and non-empty.
implementation.fallback: When the trusted root is unavailable the measured verification runs unchanged through the TUF cache, so verification never weakens.

limitations: Measurements were taken on ntnu against a public keyless-signed image; the private runner measured 3.263s for the equivalent private verification on 2026-09-22, so the absolute saving on the runner is not directly established by this file.
Five samples per variant on one host; no percentile claim.
The runner-side effect is qualified separately by the llunde-pyparser production canary that follows this change.
